requirements.summary: Each job is counted as passed, failed or incomplete. A time limit or a job that never started is incomplete and never a pass.

New, reopened, closed and open defects are counted per campaign; a reopened defect is not new, a fix counts in the campaign that verified it, and environment trouble is kept apart from circuit and testbench defects.
Functional and code coverage are reported separately, only from jobs that passed, with the number of jobs left out and every change of denominator.
A job is flaky when the same plan (commit, seed and profile) gave both a pass and a fail; a different seed is a different plan, and an incomplete run is not a verdict.
Defects found after the last campaign are listed as escapes with the check that should have found them.
The closure check lists every criterion that is not met; it does not approve anything.
A history with a missing or repeated result, decreasing dates, an unknown campaign, an impossible issue history or impossible coverage is refused with a stable label.
The table, its independent recount and the Markdown a reviewer reads agree, also on generated histories.
